bull.b: The Anthropic lease materially improves revenue visibility and supports a durable shift toward AI infrastructure. Its long term, large capacity commitment can anchor future utilization, strengthen customer credibility, and support financing for additional power-constrained data center development.

bull.t: Rapid HPC leasing growth and capacity expansion
bull.b: HPC leasing is becoming the company’s primary revenue engine, with growth supported by commissioned Lake Mariner capacity and additional facilities under construction. Increasing contracted capacity should diversify revenue beyond Bitcoin mining and improve the business model’s scalability.

Substantial liquidity and proceeds from selling the Abernathy interest provide funding for committed construction and strategic expansion. Recycling capital from a joint venture into larger controlled assets can improve execution focus while reducing dependence on near-term equity financing.

bear.t: Deep operating losses and weak profitability
bear.b: Large losses show that gross profit is not yet covering operating, development, financing, and other costs. Although new HPC capacity may improve economics, sustained negative EBITDA indicates the platform remains dependent on successful execution and future revenue ramp-up.

bear.t: High cash burn and strained capitalization
bear.b: The business is not currently self-funding and requires substantial investment to complete its infrastructure build-out. Negative cash generation, thin reported equity, and high leverage reduce financial flexibility and could increase refinancing, dilution, or project funding risk.

bear.t: Execution risk and near-term margin pressure
bear.b: Scaling multiple complex data center projects requires scarce electrical labor and customer-specific design work, creating schedule and cost risks. The gap between reported and targeted margins also indicates that economics may remain pressured until capacity is completed and pre-revenue costs decline.
